About creatures

Creatures are summoned with creature spells and fight for their hero.

Power and toughness

Each creature has power, the damage it deals in combat, and toughness, the damage it can take. Damage on a creature heals at the end of each turn, so a creature is destroyed only when it takes as much damage as its toughness within one turn.

Resting

A creature that attacks or uses certain abilities rests and stays down until its owner's next turn. A newly summoned creature also rests unless it has Haste. Resting creatures cannot block.

Abilities

Most creatures have abilities, shown as icons. See Creature abilities for the common ones and Attack and defence for how they affect combat.

Limits

A hero can control at most 10 creatures. Destroyed creatures go to their owner's graveyard; some spells bring them back.

All creatures of both games: the list of creatures.

Preview animations and sounds

Press F6 in the game and open a page from the creature list. Use the menu below the 3D model to choose an animation, then press Play. Depending on the creature, you can preview attacks, ranged attacks, hit reactions, deaths, and other actions. To return to the idle pose, select Idle and press Play again.

Drag the model to turn it and scroll to zoom. When the page offers models for both games, choose Etherlords I or Etherlords II to see the animations available in that edition.

The viewer plays the original creature sounds when a recording is available. It uses the Effects volume from Options. The web wiki shows still images of creatures.
